title: Tiered-approximate-reads-and-adaptive-connection-throttle-for-downstream-resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: During regional failovers and downstream overloads (Redis/Kafka/Postgres) we've observed cascading retries and connection queue buildup that pushes tail latencies above SLOs and causes hard failures for non-essential read paths. Goal: implement a coordinated, tiered degradation strategy that (1) allows best-effort 'approximate' reads (stale/partial/hashed-sampling) for low-value routes, (2) applies an adaptive per-tenant connection throttle and lease allocator to prevent head-of-line blocking, and (3) exposes clear circuit-breaker and fallback semantics so runtime and Console can route or degrade features gracefully. This ticket wires together the runtime-side control loop, new read-mode flags, and traffic shaping hooks in the connection broker.
acceptance_criteria: Service p95 token-generation latency does not increase by more than 10% under simulated downstream 2x load when tiered-approx reads are enabled for low-priority routes

Under a synthetic Redis outage in us-west-2, high-priority requests maintain >=99.5% success (no degraded stub), low-priority requests fall back to approximate reads with documented consistency semantics
Connection queue length for downstream clients (per-host) stays bounded and recovers within 90s after overload with adaptive throttle enabled
Console shows per-route degrade level and number of approximate-read hits, and rollout can toggle degrade levels by route
Automated smoke tests and chaos scenarios demonstrate no SLO regression for dedicated-capacity customers in the testbed
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated in runtime (off by default). 2) Canary to 10% of traffic in staging with synthetic Redis/Kafka overload profiles. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% while monitoring p50/p95/p99 and error budgets. 4) Expand to 50% then 100% if metrics stable. 5) Expose per-tenant knob in Dedicated and Private via Console after safe canary.
metrics_and_slos: primary_slo: 99.9% successful generation requests (<= 1500ms) - must hold across canary
p95_latency: track pre/post enable and under overload profiles
connection_queue_length: alert if > 100 for > 30s per host
approx_read_rate: % of total reads served by approximate path
fallback_rate: % of requests served by stub/backfill vs. full downstream read
implementation_notes: New runtime read modes: fresh, cached-stale, sampled-approximation, stub
Adaptive throttle implemented in connection-broker with per-tenant token-bucket + lease expiry
Circuit breaker state warmup: conservative open thresholds during canary, accelerate after stable telemetry
Preserve KV cache semantics: approximate reads read from a compacted in-memory prefix cache where possible
Telemetry: add span attributes for degrade_level and degrade_reason to tie to existing tracing
testing_plan: Unit tests for read-mode selector and token-bucket behavior
Integration test injecting artificial Redis/Kafka latency and verifying degrade path correctness
Load tests in staging using the fault-injection harness (redis-delay, tcp-reset)
Chaos run: region failover (us-west->us-east) while degrade mode active; measure tail latency and error budgets
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Approximate reads could surface incorrect results to customers - Mitigation: label responses with 'approximate' flag and provide opt-out per-tenant
Risk: Adaptive throttle may penalize bursty-but-legitimate tenants - Mitigation: tenant-weighted buckets + emergency override for admin agents
Risk: Cache growth due to approximate path - Mitigation: bounded TTL and LRU eviction plus instrumentation to cap memory impact
Risk: Operational complexity - Mitigation: add clear Console controls and runbook for rollback
